The 10 metre DTM is a raster elevation model.
It is resampled from the 2 metre composite DTM.
The 2 metre source is resampled using bilinear interpolation.
It ultimately derives from last or only LiDAR returns.
Surface objects are removed in the terrain-model workflow.
Repeat surveys use the newest suitable best-resolution data.
The 2 metre DSM is a raster elevation model.
The surface model includes vehicle heights.
The surface model includes building heights.
The surface model includes vegetation heights.
The surface model includes the terrain surface.
The survey period runs from 6 June 2000 to 2 April 2022.
The 1 metre DSM is a raster elevation model.
It includes vehicles, buildings and vegetation.
The data is available as GeoTIFF rasters.
The first-return 1 metre DSM is a raster elevation model.
It uses the first or only laser return.
It includes terrain where the first or only return was the ground.
It derives from National LiDAR Programme surveys.
The survey period runs from 11 November 2016 to 5 May 2022.
The programme divided England into about 300 survey blocks.
Survey capture was undertaken over continuous winters.
Its coverage need not match the last-return DSM composite.
The first-return 2 metre DSM is a raster elevation model.
WCS is an OGC standard for serving multidimensional coverages.
WCS can be used in QGIS.
WCS can be used in Esri ArcGIS Desktop.
WCS can return raw pixel values such as elevation.
WCS is available for LiDAR composite elevation models.
WCS is available for the SurfZone DEM.
WCS is available for the Vegetation Object Model.
WCS and WMS replace Esri image services using open formats.
ArcGIS WCS does not provide raster statistics automatically.
ArcGIS displays WCS rasters using stretch rendering.
The published DTM 1 m minimum statistic is -409.05.
The published DTM 1 m maximum statistic is 978.05.
The published DTM 2 m minimum statistic is -408.88.
The published DTM 2 m maximum statistic is 977.99.
The published first-return DSM 1 m maximum statistic is 979.63.
The published first-return DSM 2 m maximum statistic is 979.58.
WCS GeoTIFFs use -3.4028235e+38 as the NoData value.
ArcGIS Pro users can use dynamic range adjustment for the current screen extent.
ArcGIS Pro users can use the Make WCS Layer tool.
OS Terrain 5 is a mid-resolution DTM.
It is designed to interoperate with large-scale OS data.
It is published as grid and contour data.
Grid and contour products use the same source data.
Both products are supplied in 5 km by 5 km tiles.
The grid has regular 5 metre post spacing.
Standard contours use 5 metre vertical intervals.
Index contours occur at 25 metre intervals.
Contours include mean high and mean low water boundaries.
The product is maintained through an integrated 3-to-5-year flying programme.
